question.text: Will at least one of the two Ir-192 sources stolen from the Rivers State radiography facility be publicly confirmed recovered by 28 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, as of 28 November 2026 (23:59 UTC), Nigerian federal or Rivers State authorities (including the Nigeria Police Force) have publicly stated that at least one of the two Ir-192 radioactive sources stolen from the industrial radiography facility in Rivers State — the theft disclosed by the NNRA in its press release of 9–11 November 2026 — has been recovered, meaning the radioactive material itself is back under the control of the authorities or the licensed operator. A statement by the licensee or operator alone does not count, and neither does a statement that only empty source projectors or the transit container were recovered. The primary resolution source is the NNRA news and press-release page at https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news; if no qualifying statement is posted there, a report by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) attributing such a statement to those authorities also counts. The question is judged on the state of the public record at that cutoff, so the date on which a qualifying confirmation was issued does not affect the outcome; if no qualifying public confirmation exists as of the cutoff, the question resolves No.
question.fine_print: A statement reporting recovery of only some of the six projectors counts only if it indicates that the Ir-192 material was inside them (for example, that the recovered units were intact) or that the sources themselves were recovered. An arrest, a charge, or a statement that the material has been "located" or "traced" but not yet retrieved does not count; a statement that the stolen projectors were recovered intact, or that the Ir-192 material has been recovered or retrieved, counts as Yes.

research:
I'm writing up the findings now. As of 17 November 2026 nothing has been publicly confirmed as recovered.

## 1. Resolution source
- The NNRA news page at [nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news) was read directly on 2026-11-17. Its newest item is "NNRA, NSCDC strengthen collaboration on radiation safety, safe mining and CBRNE response in Gombe". This is about Gombe and does not mention the Rivers State theft or any recovery. The second item is still the original release, "NNRA convenes National Nuclear Security Committee meeting on reported security breach at industrial radiography facility". There is no follow-up item. The posts show no publication dates. [NNRA news](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news), [Gombe post](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra__nscdc_strengthen_collaboration_on_radiation_safety__safe_mining_and_cbrne_response_in_gombe)
- 2026-11-09 (meeting date; the release itself is undated): the release says six source projectors, two of them holding Ir-192, and one transit container were stolen from the storage pit. The NNSC "agreed on modalities for investigating… and recovering the missing equipment" and divided responsibilities among agencies. The release reports no recovery, arrests or suspects. [NNRA release](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra_convenes_national_nuclear_security_committee_meeting_on_reported_security_breach_at_industrial_radiography_facility)

## 2. Current status
- I found nothing that settles the question. No public statement from the NNRA, the police or the Rivers State government says the sources or intact projectors have been recovered. The unverified OtownGist "recovered - fully intact" claim mentioned in the background still has no confirmation from any other outlet or from the NNRA.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13 to 11-16: The Rivers State news I could find covers Navy raids on illegal refineries (56,800 litres of crude recovered). None of it mentions radioactive material. [P.M. News](https://pmnewsnigeria.com/2026/11/14/navy-discovers-56800-litres-of-stolen-crude-in-rivers-forest), [Leadership](https://leadership.ng/navy-destroys-illegal-refining-sites-recover-stolen-crude-in-rivers/)
- 2026-11-11: Nigerian outlets ran the NNRA release, according to the question background. Several extended searches for police statements, arrests or recovery reports found nothing about this incident.
- I could not find any Nigeria Police Force or Rivers State Police Command statement on the case.

## 4. Base rates (comparable Ir-192 radiography thefts)
- Stolen radiography cameras are often dumped and later found, usually within days to about two weeks. Recovery tends to be announced quickly in countries where regulators publish actively:
  - 2015, Tabasco, Mexico: an Ir-192 container was found under a bridge after a tip. [Yahoo/AFP](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/stolen-radioactive-material-recovered-mexico-official-173458595.html)
  - 2016, Mexico: an Ir-192 device was recovered in a neighbouring state about two weeks after it went missing. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2016/03/09/us/mexico-radioactive-device-recovered/index.html)
  - 2023, Guanajuato, Mexico: a stolen camera was recovered intact. [IAEA](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/mexico-informs-iaea-about-recovery-of-stolen-radioactive-source)
  - 2023, Gqeberha, South Africa: an Ir-192 canister was recovered at a scrap dealer. [Daily Maverick](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-11-14-gqeberha-police-confirm-stolen-radioactive-material-recovered-at-scrap-metal-dealer.md)
  - 2017, Malaysia: two Ir-192 projectors were stolen, eight people were arrested, and detectors were used to trace the material. [NST](https://nst.com.my/news/2017/02/212097/eight-nabbed-connection-radioactive-material-theft-case-video)
  - US cases: a camera was found with its source still locked in the shielded case. [Tulsa](https://www.newson6.com/story/5e368c822f69d76f620a3cf9/stolen-radioactive-camera-recovered-along-a-tulsa-highway)
- Some sources are never recovered. A GAO testimony cites one such case. [GAO](https://www.gao.gov/assets/gao-14-681t.pdf)
- This theft has some features that may matter:
  - It was a deliberate break-in to a storage pit, which suggests the thieves were after scrap metal or knew what they were taking.
  - The theft date is unknown, so the time already elapsed may be longer than it looks.
  - The NNRA posts irregularly and has not named the licensee.
- Nigeria's record: the NNRA has worked with the IAEA on recovery missions before. [IAEA](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/news/iaea-helps-recover-stray-radioactive-sources-nigeria)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this incident. The markets that were collected (Rivers governor 2027, Nigerian Senate, and others) are unrelated.

## 6. Upcoming events before 28 Nov
- No scheduled NNRA briefing, NNSC follow-up meeting or police press conference has been announced that I could find.
- Things that could still move the outcome:
  - an NNRA follow-up release
  - a statement from the Rivers Police Command or NSCDC
  - an IAEA mention through its incident database or news releases, though that would not count unless it is attributed to Nigerian authorities
  - Nigerian media picking up any recovery

Two caveats: the search engine indexed almost no Nigerian coverage of this incident (it did not even surface the 11 November Daily Post story), so a recovery reported only in local media could have been missed. The NNRA page should be checked again close to the cutoff.

## Research summary: stolen Ir-192 sources, Rivers State (as of 2026-11-17)

I found no public confirmation that either Ir-192 source has been recovered. The NNRA has posted no follow-up, and I could not find any news report of a recovery, arrest or police statement.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17 (checked): The NNRA news page at nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news lists one item about the incident: "NNRA CONVENES NATIONAL NUCLEAR SECURITY COMMITTEE MEETING ON REPORTED SECURITY BREACH AT INDUSTRIAL RADIOGRAPHY FACILITY". It is the second-newest post. [NNRA news](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news)
- What that release says: six source projectors were stolen from a storage pit, two of them containing Ir-192, plus one transit container. The IAEA was notified through three channels: the Incident and Trafficking Database (ITDB), the USIE information-exchange system and its Incident and Emergency Centre. The committee met on 2026-11-09 and "agreed on modalities for investigating the incident and recovering the missing equipment." The release does not mention any recovery, suspect, licensee name or theft date. [NNRA release](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra_convenes_national_nuclear_security_committee_meeting_on_reported_security_breach_at_industrial_radiography_facility)
- The only newer post is about a Gombe partnership with the NSCDC (the civil defence corps). It has nothing to do with the theft. So the NNRA has posted at least once since the release without giving an update on recovery. [NNRA Gombe post](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra__nscdc_strengthen_collaboration_on_radiation_safety__safe_mining_and_cbrne_response_in_gombe)
- The news pages show no dates on the posts, and I found no data feed or API behind them.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. There is no qualifying public statement that the sources were recovered.
- The OtownGist claim that the devices were "recovered, fully intact" is still unverified. My searches found only OtownGist's 11 November headline ("NNRA Launches Investigation After Theft of Radioactive Equipment in Rivers"), with no recovery claim. [OtownGist](https://www.otowngist.com/2025/02/house-of-representatives-considers-creation-of-31-new-states-sparking-national-debate/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13 to 15: Rivers State news in this period was about Navy raids on illegal refineries. None of it mentioned radioactive material. [National Accord](https://nationalaccordnewspaper.com/navy-dismantles-2-illegal-refining-sites-in-rivers-recovers-56800-litres-of-crude), [Vanguard](https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/navy-uncovers-68175-litres-of-suspected-stolen-crude-in-rivers/)
- 2026-11-11: Daily Post ran "NNRA summons stakeholders over theft of radioactive sources in Rivers". On 2026-11-17 it was still the newest radioactive-related story in Daily Post's search results, with no follow-up. [Daily Post search](https://dailypost.ng/search/radioactive/)
- 2026-11-17: Bing News RSS returned nothing for "NNRA radioactive Rivers" or "radioactive Rivers State theft". Google News RSS blocked my request (error 429, too many requests). I found no statement from the Rivers State Police Command.

### 4. Base rates
- Stolen radiography devices elsewhere are often found intact within days to weeks. Mexico has recovered stolen Ir-192 cameras intact in their shielding, and India's regulator reported devices stolen in October 2025 were recovered intact. [Laka INES 1066](https://www.laka.org/docu/ines/event/1066), [AERB](https://www.aerb.gov.in/storage/uploads/News/newsR6xm1.pdf), [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/mexico-issues-alert-over-stolen-radioactive-material-1.1493187)
- Nigeria's own record is slower. In the 2002-03 case, two oilfield sources went missing on 2002-12-03 and the public warning came only months later, followed by an IAEA mission to help find them. [VOA](https://www.voanews.com/a/a-13-a-2003-03-01-32-iaea-66845612/258499.html), [GlobalSecurity](https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/library/news/2003/02/mil-030228-3e1886d5.htm)
- A 2012 report said about 26 sources were abandoned in the Niger Delta between 2000 and 2011, which shows long-running gaps in source control. [Sweetcrude](https://sweetcrudereports.com/oil-firms-operating-in-nigeria-abandon-26-radioactive-substances/)
- The NNRA posts news irregularly, often weeks apart, and has published nothing on the case in the roughly 6 days since the release.
- Mexico and India announced recoveries quickly. I could not find a clear past case of the NNRA itself announcing the recovery of a stolen projector.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market or expert forecast on this incident. The markets supplied (Rivers and other governorship races, Nigerian Senate, sports) have nothing to do with it.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- No briefing or event is scheduled. Things that could move the outcome:
  - an NNRA follow-up release
  - a Rivers police or NSCDC parade of suspects (an arrest alone does not count)
  - an IAEA ITDB or USIE update (these are not public, and the IAEA is not a qualifying source unless it attributes a statement to Nigerian authorities)
- Outlets to keep watching up to 28 November: the NNRA news page and its social accounts (Facebook nnraofficial, X @nnra_official), plus Daily Post, Vanguard, Punch and the Guardian (Nigeria).

Sources: [NNRA news](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/news), [NNRA release](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra_convenes_national_nuclear_security_committee_meeting_on_reported_security_breach_at_industrial_radiography_facility), [NNRA Gombe post](https://nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-nnra__nscdc_strengthen_collaboration_on_radiation_safety__safe_mining_and_cbrne_response_in_gombe), [Daily Post search](https://dailypost.ng/search/radioactive/), [OtownGist](https://www.otowngist.com/2025/02/house-of-representatives-considers-creation-of-31-new-states-sparking-national-debate/), [National Accord](https://nationalaccordnewspaper.com/navy-dismantles-2-illegal-refining-sites-in-rivers-recovers-56800-litres-of-crude), [Vanguard](https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/navy-uncovers-68175-litres-of-suspected-stolen-crude-in-rivers/), [Laka](https://www.laka.org/docu/ines/event/1066), [AERB](https://www.aerb.gov.in/storage/uploads/News/newsR6xm1.pdf), [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/mexico-issues-alert-over-stolen-radioactive-material-1.1493187), [VOA](https://www.voanews.com/a/a-13-a-2003-03-01-32-iaea-66845612/258499.html), [GlobalSecurity](https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/library/news/2003/02/mil-030228-3e1886d5.htm), [Sweetcrude](https://sweetcrudereports.com/oil-firms-operating-in-nigeria-abandon-26-radioactive-substances/), [Guardian NG](https://guardian.ng/news/police-alert-rivers-residents-on-planned-destruction-of-expired-explosives/)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 11 days remain, until 28 November 2026 at 23:59 UTC. For Yes, Nigerian federal or Rivers State authorities (NNRA, police, NSCDC and similar) must publicly state that at least one Ir-192 source, or a projector recovered intact with its source inside, is back under control. That statement must appear on the NNRA news page or be reported by credible media attributing it to those authorities.

(b) The status quo is No. As of 17 November there is no follow-up from the NNRA, no police statement and no credible report of recovery. The NNRA has posted a newer, unrelated item (Gombe) without any update on the theft.

(c) Base rate: internationally, stolen radiography cameras are often found within days to two weeks. In countries with active regulators (Mexico, South Africa, India), quick and public recovery happens in perhaps 50-70% of cases within a month. Nigeria's record is much slower and less transparent:
- The 2002-03 missing sources took months to surface publicly.
- I could not find a clear precedent of the NNRA announcing recovery of a stolen projector.

Combining roughly 40% chance of physical recovery within the window with roughly 40-50% chance it is publicised in time gives a base rate of about 15-20%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:** The NNSC met on 9 November with security agencies and assigned recovery tasks. The IAEA was notified, which adds pressure. Stolen projectors are frequently dumped or show up at scrap dealers. There is also the unverified OtownGist "recovered fully intact" snippet, though it carries little weight.
- **For No:**
  - Six days after the release there is no follow-up, despite at least one newer NNRA post.
  - Daily Post shows no follow-up as of 17 November.
  - The theft was a deliberate break-in to a storage pit, possibly for scrap, with an unknown and possibly earlier date.
  - The NNRA posts irregularly and with lags, and publicising recoveries may be deprioritised.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The investigation continues quietly. Projectors are perhaps found later, or only empty projectors are found, and the NNRA posts nothing before 28 November.
- **Yes:** Police trace the projectors to a scrap yard in Port Harcourt, recover them with sealed sources intact, and the NNRA issues a release, or the Rivers police parade suspects alongside the devices before the cutoff.

(f) I start from about 17%. I move down slightly because of the silence so far, Nigeria's slow publicity record, the uncertain theft date and the short remaining window. I give a small credit for the active multi-agency effort and possible scrap-dealer recovery. That lands at about 12%.

Probability: 12%

(a) About 11 days remain, until 28 November 2026 23:59 UTC. For Yes, Nigerian federal or Rivers State authorities (NNRA, police, NSCDC and similar) must publicly state that at least one Ir-192 source, or a projector recovered intact with its source, is back under control. The statement must appear on the NNRA site or be credibly reported.

(b) If nothing changes, the answer is No. As of 17 November there has been no follow-up from the NNRA, no police statement and no media report of a recovery. The NNRA has posted once since the release, about Gombe, without any update.

(c) Base rate: stolen radiography cameras in countries with active regulators (Mexico, India, South Africa, the US) are recovered intact and announced within about two to three weeks perhaps 50 to 60% of the time. For Nigeria the rate is much lower. Recovery depends on finding a scrap-oriented, deliberate theft in the Niger Delta. The NNRA publishes rarely and with lags, and I know of no clear past case where it promptly announced recovering a stolen projector. Multiplying a recovery chance of roughly 35 to 45% within the window by a prompt public confirmation chance of roughly 40% gives about 15 to 20%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The NNSC met on 9 November and assigned recovery tasks.
- The IAEA has been notified, which adds pressure to find the sources.
- Thieves globally often dump projectors.
- An unverified OtownGist snippet claims the devices were "recovered, fully intact."

Evidence for No:
- Nothing has been posted on the NNRA page through 17 November, even though it has posted a newer, unrelated item.
- No Daily Post follow-up has appeared by 17 November.
- No police statement has been found.
- The theft was a deliberate pit break-in, possibly by scrap-metal thieves.
- The theft date is unknown, so more time may already have passed than it appears.
- Nigeria's history of slow source recoveries and lagging announcements points the same way.

(e) No scenario: the projectors remain missing, or are quietly retrieved and the NNRA posts nothing before 28 November, or an announcement mentions only arrests. Yes scenario: a tip leads police to dumped projectors in a creek or scrapyard, and the NNRA or the Rivers Police Command parades suspects and states the units were found intact, which Nigerian outlets then report.

(f) I start from about 18% and move slightly down for the six days of silence and the low detection rate in Nigeria. I keep a small premium for the OtownGist rumour and for a possible quick NNRA post if a recovery happens, since recoveries are good news that agencies like to publicise.

Probability: 13%

(a) About 11 days remain, until 28 November 2026 23:59 UTC. For Yes, the NNRA, Nigerian police or another federal or Rivers State authority must publicly state that at least one Ir-192 source has been recovered, or that projectors holding the sources were recovered intact. Credible media attributing such a statement to those authorities also counts.

(b) If nothing changed, the outcome is No. As of 17 November there is no follow-up from the NNRA, no police statement and no media report of a recovery.

(c) Base rate:
- Physical recovery: in countries with active regulators, stolen radiography cameras are often recovered within days to a couple of weeks. That is perhaps 50-60% within about 3-4 weeks of the theft being reported.
- Prompt publicity in Nigeria: the NNRA posts irregularly, and announcements often lag the event. I found no clear precedent of the NNRA quickly announcing the recovery of a stolen projector.
- Combined: roughly 20-25% that a public confirmation appears inside this window.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - The NNSC met on 9 November and assigned recovery responsibilities.
  - The IAEA was notified, which raises pressure to resolve the case.
  - The sources have little resale value, so dumping and retrieval are common.
  - There is the unverified OtownGist claim of a recovery "fully intact".
- For No:
  - The NNRA has posted at least one unrelated item (Gombe) since the release, with no update.
  - Daily Post had no follow-up as of 17 November.
  - The theft was a deliberate break-in to a storage pit taking six projectors, which suggests scrap thieves. They may dismantle the units or sell them across the Niger Delta scrap network.
  - The theft date is unknown, so more time may already have passed than it appears.
  - Nigeria's historical recoveries have been slow.

(e) Scenarios:
